changes: S0 (frozen contract, SERIAL-first) of the adversarial-review build program (docs/adversarial-review-spec.md §5): a new types-only module packages/main/src/core/adversarial-review.ts encoding the spec's frozen schemas — Finding (severity BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR + title/file/line/issue/fix, §2.2), Verdict (isReal + agreedSeverity BLOCKER|MAJOR|MINOR|NOT_A_DEFECT + reasoning, §2.3), CANONICAL_LENS_SET (6 entries with ids VERBATIM from §2.1: concept/scope, code-quality, behavior/correctness, test-coverage, crash-safety/edge, docs-consistency; task-tunable), CompletenessCriticIO (§2.4), and the review-mode interface REVIEW_MODE_PHASES (the single declared canonical 5-step order lenses->verify-lens-findings->critic->verify-critic-findings->converge-or-reopen, §2.4/§3.2/§4.2) + RoundResult/ReviewModeRound. Types/const/interfaces only — ZERO behavior (the finding_add critical|high|medium|low ledger mapping is S2, deliberately absent). A 29-assertion hermetic smoke pins every contract value to explicit literal expected tuples (drift fails). Every later story (S1-S4) imports this surface unchanged.
usage: S1-S4 import from packages/main/src/core/adversarial-review.ts: S1 (lens-runner) uses Finding + CANONICAL_LENS_SET + LensId; S2 (verifier) uses Verdict + the severity unions (and adds the finding_add ledger mapping); S3 (critic) uses CompletenessCriticIO; S4 (escalation) uses RoundResult + REVIEW_MODE_PHASES. No story needs a schema change.
expectedOutcome: Importing core/adversarial-review.ts yields the frozen types; node packages/main/dist/tasks/adversarial-review-contract-smoke.js prints 'adversarial-review-contract smoke passed: 29 assertions' (exit 0); lattice validate all green; tsc clean.
actualTranscript: tsc clean; the contract smoke prints 29 assertions (exit 0); lattice validate all 13 commands green. 2-round genuine dual-host review (Codex + Claude concept/quality lanes) resolved 4 findings: 2 MAJOR — the lens ids were hyphenated but the frozen spec §2.1 uses slash forms (string literals, so verbatim match required; Codex correctly overruled the Claude lane's 'invalid identifier' defense), and the lens-id smoke was self-referential/vacuous (now pinned to explicit literal expected tuples); 2 MINOR — the smoke didn't runtime-construct CompletenessCriticIO + ReviewModeRound. Round-2 both hosts PASS.
outcomeDiff: none — the frozen contract matches the spec §2/§3 verbatim (delivery review verified 7/7 promises); types-only confirmed; the smoke is a real drift-guard.
limitations: S0 is the frozen contract (types + interface) ONLY. The behavior — lens-runner (S1), adversarial verifier + finding_add ledger mapping (S2), completeness-critic role (S3), escalation-flow integration (S4) — is the rest of the §5 program. The first-class CLI review mode + dedicated lattice-review-completeness lane + structured verdict storage are FUTURE (§4.4).
pitfalls: A FROZEN contract must match the spec VERBATIM — lens ids are STRING LITERALS, so the spec's slash forms (concept/scope) are valid and required; hyphenating them (assuming 'slashes invalid in identifiers' — wrong for string values) creates a translation layer that breaks the no-downstream-schema-change acceptance. A contract smoke must pin assertions to EXPLICIT literal expected tuples declared in the smoke, never self-reference the module's own const (else a contract drift passes vacuously). Keep the abstract methodology severity (BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR) separate from the finding_add ledger enum (that mapping is a later story).
